newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore shares end down but dealers encouraged.
newsitem.headline: Singapore shares end down but dealers encouraged.

text.p: Singapore shares ended down on Monday, but dealers said positive signs of support were emerging that were likely to keep the main index in a tight trading range and prevent further slippage.
"The Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) is holding at 2,170 and that's a good sign," said one local dealer.
The benchmark STII closed down 5.79 at 2,172.48, recovering from a drop of more than 10 points in the morning session.
"There are some positive signs coming through now," said the dealer, who added that corporate results announced so far in the reporting season were mainly within expected ranges.
However, a volume of 209.1 million shares produced 289 losers against 104 gainers, with motor dealer Cycle & Carriage the leading faller, down Singapore $0.40 at S$14.40.
Analysts said Cycle & Carriage 1996 earnings, expected on Wednesday, were likely to be hit by low car quotas.
Shares in Singapore Telecommunications were also hit, closing down S$0.06 at S$3.22 on news it was pulling out of a bid for a cellular phone licence in India's Tamil Nadu state.
Gainers were led by Singapore Press Holdings' foreign share tranche, up S$0.50 at S$28.50.
